# Churchill Downs Thanksgiving Day Update: Coach Pope, Tiger Baby Lead Nine for McPeek on Saturday's Stars of Tomorrow II


## Nov 26, 2026


Trainer Kenny McPeek is set for a big Saturday at Churchill Downs with nine 2-year-olds entered on the 12-race Stars of Tomorrow II card, led by Grade I-placed colt Coach Pope and five-length debut winner Tiger Baby, who returns on eight days’ rest.


McPeek could tie D. Wayne Lukas’ record of four Kentucky Jockey Club victories when Coach Pope and stablemate Real Goodbar compete in the 100th running of the $400,000 race (Grade II). McPeek previously won with Repent (2001), Signalman (2018) and Smile Happy (2021).


Coach Pope, the 2-1 morning-line favorite, broke his maiden by 12 ½ lengths at one mile Sept. 12 in his only start at Churchill Downs. The son of Tapit, owned by Gainesway Stable, Shamrock Stables and Mike Mackin, went on to finish second to American History in the $650,000 Breeders’ Futurity (GI) and fourth behind unbeaten Hughes in the $2 million Breeders’ Cup Juvenile (GI), both at Keeneland. Manny Esquivel rides from post 2.


“He’s still learning. He seems to do his best running in the middle of the race right now,” McPeek said. “Manny’s been getting him in behind horses in the mornings so he can get used to taking dirt and learn to relax. He’s one for one at Churchill. This is a good race to win but it’s also a good opportunity to get him ready for some of the big races next year.”


Bayview Stables, Mark Edwards, Mike Trout, Mas Racing and Magdalena Racing’s Real Goodbar returns to dirt after winning the $250,000 Thoroughbred Aftercare Alliance Stakes by three lengths on turf at Keeneland on Oct. 30. He finished fourth in the $300,000 Iroquois (GIII) at Churchill Downs in his only dirt start in September. Luis Saez rides from post 9.


“He’s by Authentic and he seems to handle the dirt just fine,” McPeek said. “He’s done more on the grass so far, but we want to give him another chance on dirt against some tougher horses and see what he can do.”


Shortleaf Stable’s Tiger Baby will try two turns for the first time in the $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (GII) eight days after winning her Nov. 20 debut at one mile at Churchill Downs. John Ed Anthony’s operation bred the filly and campaigned both her sire, Plainsman, and her Arkansas-bred dam, The Mary Rose, to stakes wins at Oaklawn. Esquivel has the return mount from post 7.


“We’ve had some luck bringing horses back quick, and she came out of that race in good shape,” McPeek said Sunday. “The way she broke her maiden, I thought, why not give her a shot if everything goes right between now and the weekend? I’m thankful to have owners like Shortleaf Stable who give me the chance to make that kind of call.”


McPeek, who won the Golden Rod with Kathmanblu in 2010, also entered David Bernsen and Steve Crabtree’s Juana Margarita. The filly gets another shot at Godolphin’s Wharfie, who beat her by three-quarters of a length in the $200,000 Rags to Riches on Oct. 25. Brian Hernandez Jr. rides Juana Margarita from post 3.


Coach Pope (40-1) is one of four McPeek trainees listed in Kentucky Derby Future Wager Pool 2, which runs from noon Thursday to 6 p.m. Sunday. He’s joined by Fleetfoot Mac (75-1), Mystik Bayou (99-1) and Twinkle Town (75-1).


Fleetfoot Mac also runs Saturday, making his first start around two turns in the $140,000 Oaklawn Sports Overnight Stakes after winning his Oct. 11 debut at Keeneland. Mystik Bayou, the half-brother to Kentucky Derby 150 winner Mystik Bayou who was third in the Street Sense (GIII) at Churchill Downs, is pointing to the Dec. 5 Remsen (GII) at Belmont Park. Unbeaten Saratoga Special (GII) winner Twinkle Town is planning to return as a 3-year-old, according to McPeek.

First post for Saturday’s 12-race card is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern). The Golden Rod goes as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. with the Kentucky Jockey Club scheduled as Race 12 at 6:26 p.m.


ASMUSSEN GIVES MAIDEN MONNIE A CHANCE IN KENTUCKY JOCKEY CLUB – A month after winning the Street Sense (GIII) with Jas, Chris Hicks’ Red Lane Thoroughbreds and trainer Steve Asmussen will give the maiden Monnie his first stakes test in Saturday’s 100th running of the $400,000 Kentucky Jockey Club (GII) at Churchill Downs.


Monnie has finished second in two of his three starts, most recently behind fellow entrant Fools Rush In in a one-mile maiden race on the same Oct. 25 card that featured Jas’ Street Sense win. Keith Asmussen rode both colts that day and will be back aboard Monnie.


“I’m using Jas as a measuring stick for him,” Asmussen said. “Chris Hicks owns both of these colts and they’ve worked together countless times. I decided to give Jas some more time and let Monnie get the chance to step up.”


Earlier on the Stars of Tomorrow II card, Asmussen will send Winchell Thoroughbreds’ Dazzling back to dirt in the $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (GII). The Tapit filly has made four starts on turf since her June 28 debut at Churchill Downs. She broke her maiden at Kentucky Downs and finished second in an Oct. 9 allowance at Keeneland under Jose Ortiz, who retains the mount.


“She’s been training well over the dirt here at Churchill and has given a lot of indications that she’s going to run a very good race,” Asmussen said. “We had run her on the turf with the financial opportunities over at Kentucky Downs. She had a little success over there but plenty of time since then. We’ve always considered her a really classy filly and expect her to be an even better 3-year-old. I think this is a very good measure of where we’re at now.”


Asmussen swept the two races in 2019 with Silver Prospector in the Kentucky Jockey Club and Finite, who was co-owned by Winchell Thoroughbreds, in the Golden Rod. Asmussen also won the Kentucky Jockey Club with Private Vow in 2005 and Tapiture in 2013. A win by Monnie would tie D. Wayne Lukas’ race record of four.


The Golden Rod goes as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. and the Kentucky Jockey Club goes as Race 12 at 6:26 p.m. First post is 1 p.m.
